scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W020 contains no identifiable human figure — the observations describe organic dome-like forms, dripping verticals, and a central glow, not a figure with a body. Its role as an 'edge-dissolving figure' was unsupported. Reassigned to an honest contrasting role as a field-only composition that sets up the silhouette chapter by contrast.

W258 is visibly a large skeletal/robotic figure that fills most of the frame against a black ground — it is not a small contained figure. The draft's closing chapter framed it as 'close and contained' which is accurate, but the claim that it 'holds its ground in deep black space' with a 'raised hand the only outward gesture' is supportable. However the draft described it as 'compact' when it visually dominates its frame. Corrected to 'fills the frame'.

W265 anchor image confirms the form is a snail (coiled shell with a small head and cross-marked eyes), not an abstract coiled form. The draft's 'cross-marked points read as weary or dazed' is an unsupported emotional claim about expression. Corrected to describe visible cross marks without claiming expression.

W237 anchor image confirms the background is open pastel washes (blue, pink, lavender) with blocky outlines at lower corners and a wire/line along the top — not 'soft color washes keep the ground open' which is accurate, but the draft also said 'the figure's reach claims the horizontal space' — this is supportable from the visible extended arm reaching to the disc at right. Retained with minor wording.

W250 is visibly an animal figure (bear or similar) inside a dark inner rectangle with bokeh-like light circles in the outer field — the draft called it a 'hunched figure' which is acceptable, but 'head down, limbs pulled inward' overstates posture detail at this resolution. Softened to what is visible: a dense figure within a dark frame, outer field glowing with soft circles.
The draft transition from W265 to W237 (chapter 3 opening) referenced W265's form as 'closed and still' versus W237's extended arm — this is visually supported and retained.
The draft chapter 2 transition from W020 to W106 described W020 as having 'crowded edges' — this is visible and supported. Retained.
W003 is correctly described: hat-dominated figure with dissolving pale circles. The 'face partly hidden beneath the hat's shadow' is visible. Supported.
W106 is correctly described: black dog silhouette lower right, vast blue field, yellow zigzag marks. Supported.
W220 is correctly described: small black silhouette, raised arm, yellow field, wavy lines from head. Supported.

Reordering: W020 moved to open Chapter 1 as a field-without-figure contrast, followed by W003 as the first figure whose edges dissolve — this creates a cleaner opening progression from pure field to dissolving figure. All 8 slots retained exactly once.
Removed stock phrase 'room to breathe' from chapter prose. Removed 'like sound made visible' metaphor from W106 description. Removed 'pressure or noise' unsupported reading from W265 whyHere.
W258 described as filling its frame rather than 'compact' to match visible image.
evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change
evidence.assistantWordingScope: Specificity and overstatement corrections to exhibition headings and invitations. Existing image-reviewed memberships, chapter order and artwork roles remain intact.
evidence.referenceExpansionMethod: Exact collection-plan slot to title and CID lookup; no new interpretation

title: A Figure in Open Space
question: What changes when a figure has room around it?
introduction: Look at the space around a form before concentrating on its features. This short gallery moves from a landscape-like image and a softly layered head toward small silhouettes, larger figures and dark surroundings. Compare the amount of open ground with the scale of each subject. The relationship can change even when a character remains easy to recognize.
closing: Return to one of the smaller silhouettes after looking at a larger figure. What does the extra surrounding space make you notice?

chapters.title: Where the Figure Begins
chapters.introduction: The exhibition opens with a work offering almost no figure — only a field of organic forms and a lit center — before introducing a figure whose edges actively dissolve into its ground.

stops.whyHere: Rounded forms press in from all edges while a pale center holds open; there is no stable figure here, only a field in tension with itself — establishing the question of where a figure ends and its ground begins.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #20

stops.whyHere: A hat-and-face emerge from overlapping pale circles; the figure is present but its outline trades places with the background, answering nnxyz nnotb #20's field-only tension by introducing a figure that cannot fully separate from its ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where nnxyz nnotb #20 offers only a crowded field with a lit center and no clear figure, nnxyz nnotb #115 introduces a figure — but one whose edges dissolve into the same kind of diffuse, overlapping forms.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #115

chapters.title: Silhouette Against Open Color
chapters.introduction: Three works strip the figure to a flat black shape set against a single saturated ground, showing how much a solid form can hold when surrounded by unbroken color.

stops.whyHere: A black dog silhouette stands in the lower-right corner of a vast blue field; yellow zigzag marks radiate from it, the only marks of energy in an otherwise empty expanse.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After nnxyz nnotb #115's dissolved edges, nnxyz nnotb #212 moves to the opposite extreme — a hard black silhouette with no ambiguity at its border, set against a flat blue field that offers it almost no company.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #212

stops.whyHere: A small black figure raises one arm in a yellow field that fills the entire canvas; wavy lines fan from its head, but the yellow above remains unbroken and vast.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both nnxyz nnotb #212 and nnxyz nnotb #130 use a flat black silhouette against a single saturated ground, but nnxyz nnotb #130 centers its figure lower and surrounds it with even more uninterrupted field above.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #130

stops.whyHere: A black snail form rests on a black ground strip; mixed straight and zigzag lines burst from behind its shell into yellow, yet the large empty upper field above makes the radiating marks feel small against the surrounding space.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #130's figure reaches upward into open yellow; nnxyz nnotb #101's snail form turns inward, its shell enclosing a spiral while the same yellow field above remains unbroken and dominant.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #101

chapters.title: Figures That Reach Outward
chapters.introduction: Two works show figures extending into the picture plane — one gripping an object across open ground, one whose dense marks fill a framed interior while light drifts outside it.

stops.whyHere: A standing figure extends one arm across the composition to grip a tangle of lines leading to a glowing red disc; the open pastel washes behind it keep the ground light, making the figure's horizontal reach the dominant spatial event.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where nnxyz nnotb #101's snail is closed and low, nnxyz nnotb #146's figure stands upright and extends an arm across the width of the image, actively measuring the space around it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #146

stops.whyHere: A dense figure sits inside a dark inner rectangle while soft light circles drift across the warm outer field; the visible frame within the image divides the surrounding space into an inner zone of dense marks and an outer zone of diffuse glow.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #146's figure stands in open, undivided space; nnxyz nnotb #97 introduces a literal frame within the image, splitting the field into a dark interior and a glowing exterior.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #97

chapters.title: Figure Against Darkness
chapters.introduction: The final work removes the open field almost entirely, placing a figure against near-total black so that its own surface becomes the only available light.

stops.whyHere: A large skeletal figure fills the frame against deep black; white and orange lines trace its limbs and skull from within, so the figure carries its own light rather than drawing it from any surrounding field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #97's figure sits inside a dark rectangle with a glowing field visible beyond it; nnxyz nnotb #26 removes that outer glow entirely, leaving the figure surrounded by black with only its own traced edges providing light.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #26
